decisions.reason: The B-roll requirement does not change the caption-font standard; the source's separate lettering instruction is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.

Mixing B-roll into the full lesson does not change the existing requirement that each clip present a complete standalone lesson; the incomplete lesson observed in this message is already represented as a runtime failure.
Requiring B-roll in each video does not alter the clean, simple visual-editing style or its prohibited treatments.
The B-roll integration change has no necessary effect on the white-text-only and no-text-effects rules.
The source identifies a 45-second clip as ending too early but does not change the existing 70-to-85-second duration rule; the observed duration failure is already represented.
The per-video B-roll requirement does not change background-music selection or volume.
The instruction to mix B-roll into a full lesson does not change the existing requirement to select substantive source moments.
The B-roll rule changes an editing requirement for each clip, not the assigned batch count or the obligation to create and submit the batch.
The source changes how B-roll must be integrated but does not alter which long-form source videos may be selected or the source-exclusion rule.
The new B-roll requirement does not change the need for client approval before publication or the approving authority.
The B-roll integration instruction does not change the hook-selection criterion.
The B-roll editing standard does not change the monthly approved-clip target, counting basis, approval authority, or rejected-clip treatment.
